title: Markov Chains, section 1.9 Time reversal
version: Author's online copy of section 1.9, 5 pages, PDF dated 2001; book: Cambridge University Press 1997 (printed text not compared)
locator: Theorem 1.9.1 (time reversal of a chain in equilibrium, reversed matrix pi_j p^_ji = pi_i p_ij); definition of detailed balance; Lemma 1.9.2; Theorem 1.9.3 (reversible iff detailed balance); Example 1.9.4 (3-cycle with 2/3 and 1/3, uniform invariant law, not reversible)
assumptions: Irreducible stochastic matrix with an invariant distribution; chain started in that distribution; discrete time, countable state space.
conclusion: The time reversal of a chain in equilibrium is a Markov chain with the reversed matrix; a chain is reversible exactly when matrix and distribution are in detailed balance.
proof_status: Proofs given in the text and read. Not re-derived, but the script's examples agree (E1 is Example 1.9.4).
dependencies: Theorem 1.1.1 of the same book, not read.
relevance: Source for Proposition 3(a), the reversed kernel K*, and example E1.
limits: Read from page images of a bitmap-font PDF; one section only. Does not treat entropy production or reversal with a relabelling of states.

title: Time's Barbed Arrow: Irreversibility, Crypticity, and Stored Information
version: arXiv:0902.1209v1, 7 February 2009, 4 pages, all read; published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 103, 094101 (published text not compared)
locator: p.1 (causal states as classes of pasts with equal conditional law of the future); p.2 (h_mu^- = h_mu^+; Theorem 1, E = I[S^-;S^+]; C_mu^+ = E + H[S^+|S^-]); p.3 (causal irreversibility Xi = C_mu^+ - C_mu^-; crypticity; Corollary 1); p.4 (random insertion process, C_mu^+ ~ 1.5219, C_mu^- ~ 1.8464)
assumptions: Stationary stochastic processes over a discrete measurement alphabet.
conclusion: Authors' claims: a stationary process is equally predictable in either scan direction; the memory needed to predict and to retrodict can differ, and Xi measures the difference.
proof_status: Letter; Theorem 1 argued from an information diagram, details deferred to their references. Not re-derived. The script reproduces only the arithmetic of the two published state distributions.
relevance: Prior art for 'what matters' in fixing in distribution (Proposition 3(c)) and for the answer to question 2 with coarse readings.
open_questions: The paper defines Xi = C_mu^+ - C_mu^- and reports Xi ~ 0.3245 for values that give -0.3245; I read this as a magnitude.
limits: Says nothing about detailed balance, entropy production or exact (probability-one) functions. Same paper as the fixing-exchange lane's record; read again here.

title: Information Symmetries in Irreversible Processes
version: arXiv:1107.2168 as rendered by ar5iv (version number not recorded); sections III.2, IV.2, V.4 and VI.1 read in extracted text; the rest not read
locator: Sec. III.2, eqs. (1)-(4) (reversible process: every word as probable as its reversal; a stationary finite Markov process is reversible iff its chain is in detailed balance; time-reversed chain); Sec. IV.2, eq. (6) and footnotes (detailed balance for hidden Markov models is not equivalent to reversibility); Sec. V.4 (microscopic reversibility M+ = M-, causal reversibility C+ = C-, reversibility under symbol isomorphism; the ABC process); Sec. VI.1, eqs. (10)-(14) and Table 1
assumptions: Stationary processes with finite-state hidden Markov presentations.
conclusion: Authors' claims: several inequivalent notions of reversibility; causal reversibility is strictly weaker than microscopic reversibility; irreversibility can be driven by support or by probabilities alone.
proof_status: The Markov detailed-balance equivalence is argued in the text in both directions and attributed to their ref. [9]. Other claims not checked.
relevance: Prior art for Proposition 3(d) (relabelling) and for the observation that a cyclic process is irreversible with equal memory in both directions (E1).
open_questions: Whether their survey or later sections treat region entropies on gapped sets of times (Proposition 2) was not checked.
limits: Partial read through an HTML-to-text extraction; the term entropy production was not found by text search in the extracted file.

title: Time reversal symmetry and collapse models
version: arXiv:1502.06830 as rendered by ar5iv (v1 assumed, not verified); abstract, Sec. I (conjecture), Sec. IV and Sec. V read in extracted text; Secs. II and III not read here
locator: Sec. I (conjecture that a set of collapse centres supports forward and backward collapsing pictures, each obeying the Born rule); Sec. IV, eqs. (52)-(61) (a stochastic rule is time independent in both directions only in equilibrium; Bayes retrodiction; pre- and post-selection); Sec. V (wave function as part of the dynamical law)
assumptions: Collapse centres as the ontology; a time-independent forward stochastic rule; existence of an equilibrium distribution for the general argument.
conclusion: Authors' claims: observed asymmetries come from the asymmetric use of initial or final boundary conditions, not from the dynamics.
proof_status: A conjecture supported by two simulated models (not read here) and the analytic argument of Sec. IV, which I followed.
dependencies: Their refs to Uffink (2010) and Bacciagaluppi (2011), not read.
relevance: Source for the reading of examples E5 and E7 and for question 3.
open_questions: Their equilibrium argument does not say whether the retrodictive rule (58) equals the forward rule; that is detailed balance, which they do not mention.
limits: Partial read through an HTML-to-text extraction. The settling lane holds a fuller record of the same paper.
